newsitem.title: UK: Gold hits new 3-1/4 year lows, eyes downside.
newsitem.headline: Gold hits new 3-1/4 year lows, eyes downside.

text.p: Gold prices fell to fresh three-year lows on Monday as investors cold-shouldered the metal in favour of booming equity markets.
Gold, down $10 from the last trading day of 1996, may be teetering on the brink of even bigger losses, analysts said.
"This is the first week of the new year and we're at three-year lows," said analyst Ted Arnold of Merrill Lynch.
"Increasingly it looks like the downside is wide open. In 1997, I think $330 looks possible."

Investors have seen little reason to put money in gold, a traditional "safe haven", as U.S. inflation remains stable and equities perform at record levels. Funds, anticipating still lower prices, have sold the market heavily "short."
Bullion fixed at $359.25 an ounce in the morning, the lowest since October 7, 1993 and down sharply from the Friday afternoon fixing of $364.00.

A fresh bout of selling by speculative investment funds on Friday sent prices rapidly lower as a strong dollar and buoyant stock and bond markets pulled money out of the already bearish precious metals markets.
Gold continued losing ground in European trading on Monday.
Values have been sinking steadily since coming off a rally last February when it hit a high of $416 an ounce.
Fear that European central banks will sell some of their gold reserves to qualify for the entry to the European Monetary Union has also dulled gold's shine.
Some analysts noted that the market was due for greater price volatility this year, as a price "stranglehold" created by holders and grantors of options was broken.
Options give the right but not the obligation to buy or sell metal at a given price.
"Once you break free of options, the fundamentals take over. The fundamentals are bearish, and the charts are turning bearish, so the funds are selling. It's a downward spiral," Arnold said.
Technical analysts agreed that historical price charts pointed to more losses for gold.

"Selling pressure has increased across this complex, forcing new lows," said technical analyst Elli Gifford, of Investment Research of Cambridge. "Despite oversold considerations, further falls are likely."
Some dealers put initial support for gold at a historical chart point around $358, while brokers Rudolf Wolff said there was little propping up values above $350 an ounce.
The other precious metals, particularly platinum, were also suffering from gold's weakness.
"All the precious metals are under the cosh and as yet they haven't found happy levels. No one wants to stand in their way down," a dealer noted.
Platinum like gold fixed at a 3-1/4 year low of $362.75 an ounce on Monday, down $3.25 from Friday's fixing.
Business was brisk, with ample sellers in the market, platinum dealers said.
Silver was steadily edging lower, indicated two cents below Friday's closing level at $4.66 an ounce.
Palladium was more buoyant than the others, but it was still fixed $2.00 lower than on Friday afternoon, at $117.75 an ounce.
